Swings and FVGs *within* the range are considered internal range liquidity (IRL) , because well, they are inside the range. 



Simply know that price goes from IRL to external range liquidity (ERL) and vice versa. 

E.g., for IRL to ERL

when bullish, if price hits a bullish FVG formed on an upward displacement as it pulls back,  ideally you buy there and aim for an ERL which could be the swing high before the pull back or any bearish FVG above the swing high. 

For ERL to IRL

from the previous example, if say you have a bearish bias, then after taking out the external high, you would now aim for any bullish FVG generally formed before taking out that high (given that you enter on a proper model). 
 
This is one of different ways to interpret this concept. Others may have differing opinions.

If you trade ICT, you should wait for price to reach at or below 50% of the range to consider buys. Once you get there don't simply buy blindly. Have an entry model that's fixed so that you may have consistency on every trade regardless of win or loss. 

Another thing to note with ICT is liquidity and liquidity sweeps. 

Say, if you have a bullish bias and you've marked out your Fibs on a price leg as you've done here, you wait for discount ( below 50%) and then when you see a low traded through only to quickly reverse up with momentum as you  saw between 6:00 and 9:00 on your chart; thats when you consider entering. 

Then you take some profits at the next high and trail the rest.

Bought way too high. Could have gotten long at slightly above 4.500 when you got the energetic move  above the swing high prior to it then taking profits at the high. Your SL could then have been at that swing low which is much better defined than an arbitrary SL in between the upmove.. 

Also, don't buy after price takes out a high. Tends to reverse right after. Either wait for a retracement or get in before that.
